:::{#thm-sigma-algebra-intersection}
#### An intersection of $\sigma$-algebras is a $\sigma$-algebra

Let $\salg_j$ be a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) on a set $S$
for each $j$ in a nonempty set of indices $J$.
Then their [intersection](sets-functions.qmd#def-intersection)
$\bigcap_{j \in J} \salg_j$,
the collection of subsets of $S$ that are in every $\salg_j$,
is a $\sigma$-algebra on $S$.

:::

::: proof

Each condition of @def-sigma-algebra holds:

- $S$ is in every $\salg_j$, so it is in the intersection.
- If $A$ is in the intersection, then $A$ is in every $\salg_j$,
  so its complement $S \setminus A$ is in every $\salg_j$,
  and so it is in the intersection.
- If $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ are in the intersection, then they are in every $\salg_j$,
  so their union $\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i$ is in every $\salg_j$,
  and so it is in the intersection.

:::
